verse.reading: If one knows the root, one can see all three worlds beforehand and reach eternal release; is there any gain in knowing a great many roots? Be clear that the world is false, and dance.
verse.nuance: The plain contrast is one root against many: knowing the single source against a herbalist's or scholar's knowledge of countless roots. மூலவேர் can also point to the root-centre (மூலம்) of the yogic body. சகத்தைப் பொய் is the Vedantic world-is-false, said flatly.

finding.claim: On the predictive-processing account, perception is the brain's best guess about the causes of sensory input, constantly corrected by prediction error.

verse.reading: So that onlookers will esteem them as eaters of kaya-kalpa, they do conjuring tricks everywhere, frauds and cheats; because they smoke ganja at set hours and eat opium straight, they roam the land like dogs, licking and sniffing.
verse.nuance: காயகாயம் is read as காயகற்பம், the body-preserving medicine of Siddha tradition; the verse says its claimants are kept going by hemp and opium instead. It is a witness to the drugs of the wandering ascetic, and treats the kaya-kalpa claim as a cover rather than denying the medicine.

finding.claim: Curcumin, though popular, is unstable, poorly absorbed and a frequent false positive in assays, and no double-blind trial has shown a clear therapeutic benefit.

verse.reading: We will shut the snake in the pot of ம, we have scooped up and eaten the breath of the jewelled circle, we will push away the pots of வ, leap past the crooked dream, let it dance in the open sea of space, offer the five instruments as sacrifice, and saying we stand become the form of சி, see the holy feet, be clear and dance.
verse.nuance: The letters are those of the five-letter mantra: in the usual Saiva reading ம stands for mala or the body, வ for grace, சி for Siva. The snake begins in ம and ends as சி, so the stanza is a passage through நமசிவாய from bond to Siva. பஞ்ச கருவி are the five senses, and வாசி is the breath as practice.

finding.claim: In two combined randomised trials, eight weeks of mindfulness training produced no structural brain changes compared with active and waitlist controls.

verse.reading: To all the men who, born human among the seven births that Brahma, son of Vishnu, arranged, do not bow at the flower feet of the mountain daughter's lord and reach the Siva-state but delight in women and celebrate love, the poet speaks, and bids the blind-eyed listen: the soles that toil over thorns and stones they call cotton; the shins that are white bone they praise as leaping varal fish; the thighs of flesh and bone they call plantain stems; the waist that carries the long body they call a drum; the belly rolling with excrement, urine, slime and wrinkles they call a banyan leaf; the breasts that spread like a spider's web, swell, ooze, are scratched by nails, dry, shrink and hang for people to laugh at they call lotus buds, 'I say this to the blind of lust'; the hands that stretch, fold, take goods, feed and knead they call kanthal flowers; the neck of sweat and grime they call the areca palm; the hot and foul mouth they call the murukku flower; the teeth that chew rice and curry they call pearls; the sharp nose that drips water and mucus they call the kumizh fruit; the eyes that run with water and rheum they call water-lilies; the ears where wax rots they praise as vallai stalks; the hair on the skull, where lice and nits breed if oil is not combed in, they call a dark cloud; and saying such things in praise they go to the gate of hell they desire, the pit of lust where skin and flesh ooze pus, the field where embryos grow, the way the menstrual flow passes, the holed gate, the great road down which the eight-span body comes, the hidden place where earthly lust is spent, the gate where the dog of lust sits desiring, the sluggish road where those without the grace of the moon-crested one linger, the sore they cover with a cloth saying 'this is a wound', the rich sore that sounds with running water, the way the deluded enter and the sick never leave, the pit the proud lechers fall into, the great road by which woman and man are born, the water gate beside the gate where excrement falls: do not say this is sweet; bow instead at the twin feet of the one Lord of Kachi, who pities his devotees even for an offered leaf and grants the release of the Siva-state, lord of release, ageless First, who saw all the worlds in all the eggs, and give up praising the women of pleasure.
verse.nuance: The method is to quote the convention and then name the referent: each limb is given first as function or matter (bone, sweat, mucus) and then as the poets' figure, so that the figure is convicted by what it covers. The second catalogue is unusually literal, and தூமைக் கடவழி, the way of the menstrual flow, uses the Siddhars' word for the womb's impurity; பெண்ணும் ஆணும் பிறக்கும் பெருவழி concedes that the same gate is the way of every birth, including the hearer's. The attack is on the eye and the convention, not on women as persons, though the text does not make that distinction itself. சிலந்தி போலக் கிளைத்து, spreading like a spider or its web, for the breasts' first growth is obscure; இடைகழி வாயில் is the vestibule gate. பச்சிலை இடினும், even for a green leaf offered, is the standard measure of the Lord's easy grace.

finding.claim: The brain's dopamine 'wanting' system can drive craving independently of 'liking', so addictive desire can grow while pleasure does not.

verse.reading: Those who wandered without seeing are crores upon crores, and those who knew the cause are crores upon crores; will one know it by wailing in vain, and what use is talking science? When without bending you set the mind at the suzhumunai, join the four to the guru's feet in the two-fours, and guard it shamelessly as one thought, the four and the eight become one: fix it and blow.
verse.nuance: The numbers are the run's cipher: tradition takes the four, the eight and the sixteen as the kalas of the breath (2432 maps them to life, pati's feet and pati), and ஊது (blow) as directing the breath. இருநான்கில் நாலைச் சேர்த்து (join the four to the two-fours) and குருபாதம் (the guru's feet, or the foot of the guru as a measure) are not explained. விஞ்ஞானம் here is discursive knowledge, not modern science.

finding.claim: Meta-analysis of small randomised trials finds alternate-nostril breathing lowers blood pressure modestly, with high heterogeneity between studies.

verse.reading: You set your love on the leather bag with nine mouths as if each day were yesterday, my heart, and wandered, having seen the cruel vultures hop and hop, strike off the shirt of skin, bite, tear, peck, cut and eat.
verse.nuance: ஒருநாளைப் போலவே, as on one day, is loving the body as if it never changed. The last line is the metre's gallop put to work, seven verbs of the vultures' eating in one breath; சட்டை, the shirt, is the skin they tear off.

finding.claim: The body replaces around 330 billion cells a day, mostly blood and gut cells, so its material is continually renewed.

verse.reading: The poet takes refuge in the Siva who held in his throat the fierce poison churned from the milk ocean, who subdued the cruel-sceptred Death with a lifted foot, who tore off a head of Brahma, maker and owner of the whole world, and holds it in his left hand, the rich lord of the golden hall; and lays before him the dream-like life that spends itself along the mind's road, the dirty mind that knows no great meaning, the thought born of anava mala and writhing in it like a worm in fat, deceit, sin, blameworthy thinking, error, envy, miserly false oaths, guile, lies, great anger, strife, murder, baseness, enmity, fear, rashness and trembling, the folly of the three gunas and the bewilderment of the five senses, trouble and disease, all packed into the body: a hut from which the bird that is life flies off, bound at the middle with bone and nerve and thatched with fat flesh, leaking, a hut of red blood and small worms, a pot of mala-body, a bag of many bodies, an endless pit of rice and sorrow, a cage where many murderous weapons lie, a rubbish heap of weary deeds, a torn sack leaking the goods of the planets, a smith's bellows that kindles the fire of anger, a cage where the birds of the five senses roost, a hollow tree where cares breed, a top spinning on the rope of desire, a windmill whirling for coins and money, a wheel confused by the deeds of its children, a cart-wheel rolled across the great void, a cruel ship that enters the sea of birth with a cargo of sin, is tossed by the wind of lust and makes the shore by the way of ruin, a grass boat moving in the shackle of the two deeds, a body that shudders when the Arbiter comes calling: when he lays this down as a corpse and sets out, he asks refuge at the lotus of the Lord's feet; refuge with the god of the white bull that charges like a thunderbolt in the open, the unblinking-eyed king, the one easy to devotees, the sea of mercy who dances in the hall of Tillai of the Vedic Brahmins and whom gods and sages praise; refuge, king of the hall, with you.
verse.nuance: The grammar carries the meaning: some thirty accusatives, the faults and the body's names alike, hang on one verb, 'when I lay it down as a corpse and set out', so that what is handed over at the refuge is everything the poet is, not a purified self. ஆணவ மலத்து உதித்து, born of anava mala, is the Siddhanta origin of the mind's own thought, and the worm in fat (நிணவைப் புழு) its figure. உயிரெனும் குருவி விட்டோடும் குரம்பை, the hut the bird of life flies from, is the Kural's image at 338 reversed, the body named from the bird's leaving. பலவுடற் புட்டில், a bag of many bodies, is loose: perhaps the body of many parts, or the body that has worn many bodies. கோள்சரக்கு, the goods of the planets, may be the planets' influence or a corrupt phrase for கோழைச் சரக்கு, phlegm. மறையவர் தில்லை, Tillai of the Brahmins, places the dance among the three thousand Dikshitars without comment, unusual in a Siddhar text that elsewhere attacks the twice-born.

finding.claim: A typical human body holds roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, so the body is in large part a community of other organisms.

verse.reading: If you can hold steady, free of the mind's modifications, the jewel-lamp that has no thought stands eternal; but if the Veda that everyone recites must babble within you, then what you saw in a dream is true: you have become clear, Sivayam.
verse.nuance: The second half can be read as irony, that taking the chanted Veda for the truth is taking a dream for real, or as a promise, that for the cleared mind even the dream is true. The first half is plain: the lamp without thought is the still mind, and it does not go out.

finding.claim: People's minds wander nearly half their waking time, and they report being less happy while wandering than while focused.

verse.reading: Making the sky a bow and the five letters an arrow, mounting the chariot of mantra to hunt the deer, in the grove where the moon and sun have gone, will I not come and play and look with a glad mind, my Mother?
verse.nuance: The deer hunt is the chase of the restless mind (மான் as deer and as the mind). Sun and moon are the two breaths in Siddhar cipher; the grove where they have gone is where the two channels end and the central one opens. The five letters are the Siva mantra.

finding.claim: Reciting a rosary prayer or a yoga mantra slows breathing to about six a minute and raises baroreflex sensitivity, linking repetitive recitation to the slow-breath physiology.

verse.reading: Joined with the adjuncts that bear names, the subtle comes in dream, and the name of the one who stands in it is Taijasa, girl of knowledge.
verse.nuance: சைதனாம் is read as தைசதன் (Taijasa), the owner of the subtle body in dream; the stanza is corrupt in lines 1 and 3.

finding.claim: Mouse studies reported that sleep increases clearance of brain waste through the glymphatic system, but a 2024 study found clearance fell during sleep, so the claim is disputed.

verse.reading: The body is impermanent; in it, infatuation is not contained by desire alone; if one stays alone, that enjoyment, standing as oneself alone, is Siva-yoga.
verse.nuance: தனித்திருந்தால், staying alone, is both solitude and the standing-as-one (தானாகி நிற்பது) that the stanza calls Siva-yoga; the enjoyment (போகம்) desire sought is redefined as the yogi's. The second line is compressed; ஆசையும் ஒன்றால் may mean that desire, being one thing, does not contain the infatuation it breeds.

finding.claim: Meta-analysis of morphometric studies reports modest structural brain differences in meditators across about eight regions, though small samples and publication bias are concerns.

verse.reading: The place where you stayed still, demon, is what was pointed to, I have told you; I do not know what maya this is, and I do not see even myself.
verse.nuance: The repetition of 1679's second half is followed by a confession: the poet does not know what the appearance is and cannot see himself. Not seeing oneself (என்னையும் காணேன்) may be failure or the goal, since 1711 denies the self altogether.

finding.claim: On the predictive-processing account, perception is the brain's best guess about the causes of sensory input, constantly corrected by prediction error.

verse.reading: When it has become rare, the eight great siddhis all eight dance; the breath merges and subsides in Brahman; front rank and back rank become one; seeing the silence that bakes and bakes, the place where one stands with the kalai changed is the golden seat; when you see yourself there is no more swimming: the way called samadhi is fixed.
verse.nuance: முன்னணி பின்னணி may be the two breaths or front and back of the body; நீச்சென்றுமில்லை, no swimming, is probably no more crossing the sea of birth; காச்சென்று காச்சிவிடும், the silence that bakes, uses the alchemist's firing for the inner heat. The sense of several words is guessed.

finding.claim: Reported evidence for precognition and other psychic powers failed to replicate and exposed weaknesses in standard statistical practice.

verse.reading: When will I stand contained within the letter a, with the letter va and the letter ma become the sword, and the letter si?
verse.nuance: The letters are those of சிவாயநம: va, ma and si are named, and அவ்வெழுத்து is the letter a (the first of Om, as the Kural's அகர முதல) or 'that letter'. The sword returns from 84: there the five letters together cut the mind, here two of them are the blade and the rest are sheathed in a. Tradition reads such letter-verses as the breath's syllables; the plain sense is the mantra folded into its first sound.

finding.claim: Case reports document severe poisoning, including cerebral edema, from Siddha capsules containing arsenic, mercury and lead thousands of times above safe limits.

verse.reading: One can ride: the silent vaasi; without covering the four or five openings, by firmness, if the mind becomes accomplished, the siddhas can gain clarity.
verse.nuance: மோனவாசி, the silent breath, is the kummi's name for the practice; பீத்தலை is obscure, read as the body's apertures that are not to be stopped, against the mouth-shutting of 2629. மனஞ் சித்தானால், if the mind becomes siddha, makes attainment a state of mind rather than a power.

finding.claim: Meditation is associated with reduced activity in the default mode network and changed coupling between it and attention and control networks, with larger effects in experienced practitioners.

verse.reading: I will speak: the left channel is the moonstone; the right channel is the sun from the first; when the light that stood lovingly in the middle departs and then becomes one without departing, that is release; for those who looked with love, this is moksha here; for those who do not see, what is there but a body of lust? As a test, draw the breath up in the left channel, hold it in the sushumna, and you will be entranced.
verse.nuance: The cipher is stated and then decoded within the verse: இடைகலை is the moon, பின்கலை the sun, and the middle light the sushumna where they unite. சோதனையாய், as a test, invites the hearer to try the kumbhaka and see; சொக்குவீரே (you will be stunned, or absorbed) is the promised result.

finding.claim: Intermittent fasting improves metabolic markers in animals and some humans, but trials show weight loss similar to ordinary calorie restriction.

verse.reading: However much sense I talked, you did not listen, good heart; why do you go astray like this and ruin yourself; like one who casts a strong hook for the fish in the sky where nothing is, you think of getting back what is gone: what sense is this?
verse.nuance: வானத்தின் மீன், the fish in the sky, is a star (மீன் means both), so the hook thrown at it is desire for what cannot be reached. போனத்தை மீள நினைத்தல், wanting back what has passed, may be lost wealth, youth or past pleasures; the verse does not say.

finding.claim: People adapt to most gains and losses so that happiness drifts back toward a personal set point, though not fully for every life event.

verse.reading: On two legs there stands a tower; staying a long time, it will sink; when one sees it, the tower stands; the Maiden lets it neither be seen nor stand, Maiden.
verse.nuance: The tower on two legs is the body; the Maiden who neither lets it be seen truly nor lets it stand is the goddess as maya, the same power that seats herself at the root. The stanza gives her both the veil and the tower's fall.

finding.claim: Reported evidence for precognition and other psychic powers failed to replicate and exposed weaknesses in standard statistical practice.

verse.reading: Those who will not gladly give plenty of food to the guests who come, yet live in prosperity, and the sinners who do not daily think of praising the name of the one who shares his body with the woman of unsucked breasts: what, asks the poet, is their being on earth?
verse.nuance: அருந்தா முலைப் பங்கர், the one who shares (the body) with her whose breasts have never been sucked, names the Lord by Uma as the virgin mother. The stanza sets feeding guests and saying the name side by side as the two duties of a householder.

finding.claim: Maximum human lifespan appears to have plateaued near 115-125 years, and radical life extension in this century is judged implausible.

verse.reading: See, a body is only the enjoyment of deeds; see, once the deeds are spent it will not stay the time of a millet grain. It joins those who think of Siva's feet and leaves those who do not. If you stand on this path, mind, is there anyone like you, my own kin?
verse.nuance: The third line is ambiguous: the subject of மேவும் and நீங்கி may be Siva's foot, which comes to those who remember it, or the body-and-deeds of the first two lines. The first reading fits the exhortation that follows; both make remembrance the hinge. The mind is called உற்றவர், one's own, in contrast to 312 where every kin is an enemy.

finding.claim: Nasal breathing entrains oscillations in olfactory and limbic brain areas and improves memory and fear recognition timed to inhalation, an effect absent with mouth breathing.

verse.reading: Having bought it, join the brain in the egg and mix in the leaf richly, son; set it inside a twisted spurge, closing the mouth of the hollow and removing the curse; when three months have gone, take out the spurge and, doing no more rite, make a seal of cloth and clay and dry it.
verse.nuance: The verse is an alchemical procedure read here for what it claims: a preparation of salt and some substance sealed in a கள்ளி (spurge) for three months, then sealed with cloth and clay for firing. அண்டத்தில் மூளை (brain in the egg, perhaps an eggshell, perhaps a skull) and வப்பிலை are unclear. சாபந் தீர்த்தே, removing the curse, is the alchemist's word for purifying a substance.

finding.claim: A scoping review found 220 cases of heavy-metal poisoning, mostly lead and mercury, linked to Ayurvedic and Siddha preparations, with most analysed samples over permissible limits.

verse.reading: Where Nandi sat is the fire-circle; the gaze fixed on the middle of the brows is the mark; the moon and the ray-sun stood in that place, jnana girl.
verse.nuance: The three lights of 2570 are now placed: fire where Nandi sits, sun and moon at the brow-centre where the gaze is held. In the cipher sun and moon are the two breaths, pingalai and idai, which meet at the brow; both the plain and the coded sense stand.

finding.claim: Meta-analysis of small randomised trials finds alternate-nostril breathing lowers blood pressure modestly, with high heterogeneity between studies.

verse.reading: Not knowing devotion I fell headlong into the void, and stayed there in agreement, as if it were a fitting sleep.
verse.nuance: The void here is a fall, not the goal of 545 and 548: without devotion the emptiness is a sleep (நித்திரை) mistaken for the state. The line is a self-question (இருந்தேண்டி?) and its grammar, ஒத்தவிட ... ஒத்தும், is awkward; the reading of 'fitting sleep' is a guess.

finding.claim: Claims that breathing through one nostril selectively activates the opposite brain hemisphere or shifts sympathetic versus parasympathetic tone rest on small, inconsistent studies.

verse.reading: Kohl-eyed wife, sons, livelihood, house: Lord of the red fire, in this world of your maya's appearances in open form, what was real day after day, as the days went by, slowly went away as a plain lie, an old tale, a dream.
verse.nuance: உருவெளித்தோற்றம், apparitions in the open, is a term for mirage-like seeing; the household is not denied but reclassified. The three words for its end, பொய், பழங்கதை, கனவு, mark a gradient from falsehood to memory to sleep.

finding.claim: Agreement between practitioners reading the pulse in Ayurvedic and Chinese medicine is low to moderate, and the methods remain poorly standardised.

verse.reading: Those who worship the Meru that is the self: if they curse, the whole cosmos burns like fire; the Meru that is honey needs initiation, and a mere boy cannot touch it; but when one who worshipped the Meru that is the sky opened his mouth and taught it, his disciple plundered the alchemical siddhi and the siddhi of the sky, the one who spoke said.
verse.nuance: Three Merus are named, தான் (self), தேன் (honey) and வான் (sky), probably grades of the same worship, but the verse does not explain them. கவன சித்தி is unclear: ககன (sky-walking) or கவனம் (attention). The last two lines are a cautionary tale about open teaching: the disciple took the powers, so the Meru is to be kept in cipher.

finding.claim: Reported evidence for precognition and other psychic powers failed to replicate and exposed weaknesses in standard statistical practice.

tamil: ஆசை கொண்ட மாதர் அடைகனவு நீக்கி உன்மேல்
verse.reading: Putting away the dream of desire I have for women, when will I take up the sound of you and subside?
verse.nuance: Desire for women is a dream (கனவு) to be ended; what replaces it is sound (ஓசை), the Lord heard rather than seen, as in 191 and 197.

finding.claim: Small randomised trials suggest ashwagandha lowers self-reported stress and anxiety, with low certainty of evidence.

verse.reading: Taking clay from a pit of filth and mixing the lump in a stream of blood, the vessel the clever potter makes is not worth even a dry stick; dance.
verse.nuance: The potter is the Lord or the father, the clay and blood the seed and the womb's blood; வறகோட்டுக்கும் ஆகாது, not worth a dry twig, is the body's price. The image is the Siddhars' and Tirumular's pot, with the making added.

finding.claim: Fasting strongly induces autophagy in animal tissues, but direct evidence that it does so in human tissues is sparse.

verse.reading: Will the place where worldly care has ceased not come to me? Will not being bewitched even by the lightning-women of the troop of impurity not come to me?
verse.nuance: மலக்குழுவின் மின்னார், women bright as lightning who belong to the company of impurity, picks up 450 to 452: freedom from their spell is asked for as a state to be given, not a discipline to be done. வசியாமை is not being charmed, the word for a spell.

finding.claim: The brain's dopamine 'wanting' system can drive craving independently of 'liking', so addictive desire can grow while pleasure does not.

verse.reading: They say the flying mercury is done, they say they have made even the needle-magnet into a cup; it is by the trickery of their world-alchemy that they make a living, girl of knowledge.
verse.nuance: கவன சூதம், mercury fixed so that it gives the power to fly (கமனம்), and the magnet worked into a vessel are boasts of the alchemical literature. புவனவாதை may be புவன வாதம், alchemy for the world's eyes, against the inner alchemy the kummi prefers.

finding.claim: Mercury can be turned into gold only by nuclear reactions such as neutron bombardment of mercury isotopes, never by chemical or alchemical processing.

verse.reading: They do not know how to bind the alkali; without turning the fierce essence into calx, by joining veesam with camphor, is it not all in vain, girl?
verse.nuance: காரம், சாரம், நீறு and பூரம் are terms of Siddha chemistry: alkali, a salt or essence (sal ammoniac in some lists), calcined powder, and camphor or borax. வீசம் is unidentified, perhaps a measure or a substance. The verse argues the order of operations matters and the ignorant skip the binding step.

finding.claim: A scoping review found 220 cases of heavy-metal poisoning, mostly lead and mercury, linked to Ayurvedic and Siddha preparations, with most analysed samples over permissible limits.

verse.reading: You fools like ghosts: will the great path that was given shape with water and limbs speak? Know within yourselves, as your own right, the God whom dark Mal and Ayan could not see.
verse.nuance: The first half is unclear. பெரியபாதை, 'the great road', may be the body, shaped from water (seed) with its limbs, which cannot speak of God; or a great ritual way. The second half is firm: the God invisible even to Vishnu and Brahma is to be realised inside, and உரிமையாக makes it one's own right.

finding.claim: Reciting a rosary prayer or a yoga mantra slows breathing to about six a minute and raises baroreflex sensitivity, linking repetitive recitation to the slow-breath physiology.

verse.reading: Inside the stench of sinew, flesh, skin and bone, not able to know the limit, the poet says he was deluded.
verse.nuance: The body is four tissues and a smell; வரம்பு, the limit or bound, is unexplained, and may be the body's own end, the measure of conduct, or the boundary between the body and the one inside it (684, 696). The stanza's pairing of the inventory with delusion is the Naladiyar's (46).

finding.claim: A typical human body holds roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, so the body is in large part a community of other organisms.

verse.reading: The teeth stand out like a crescent, the hair, matted locks and tufts grow long, the mind is dark and the form shows it; Yama's messengers come like a great mountain, cast their net and take the life; sons come bowed and weeping, the wife falls in his lap and wails that they fainted though they knew his time; neighbours say the old ones should see him, those standing by say put up the pandal and come beating the drum, asking that the corpse be burnt quickly; elders set many to work, some wash the corpse, they dress the stinking body in fine cloth, garlands and sandal and make a show of it, run crying 'lift it without breaking rank', the young sons bend and carry it, hurry to the burning ground, grieve that this is what human life is, cover it in firewood and set the fire; it burns, falls and breaks, the fat melts, the bones char and settle: a body that leaves not even a handful of ash. Rule me now, your servant who trusts you.
verse.nuance: Only the final line (நம்பும் அடியேனை இனி ஆளுமே) addresses the Lord, so the whole four-stanza life is the ground of one prayer. மாழ்கினரே இவர் காலம் அறிந்து is hard: it may be the wife's cry that they swooned though they knew his time was near, or the neighbours' comment. ஓர் பிடி நீறும் இலாத உடம்பு (a body without even a handful of ash) is the price Pattinathar sets on the body, as Arunagirinathar does.

finding.claim: Reminders of death reliably shift people's attitudes and defence of their worldviews, a moderately sized effect across many studies, though recent large replications have been weaker.

verse.reading: Food, fruit, leaf and medicine all become that very thing; those who can direct it so every day will live as long as the earth endures, and will not be caught in Death's hand.
verse.nuance: The claim is the Siddhars' kaya-siddhi: a body kept beyond death by the daily practice begun in 2415, of which this is the second half. மதுவே யாகும் (becomes that) makes whatever is eaten feed the practice rather than the body; a plain reading is that food and medicine become nectar. The verse states the claim; it does not describe a preparation.

finding.claim: The idea that a fixed stock of breaths or heartbeats sets lifespan rests on a cross-species correlation; within humans, lower resting heart rate predicts lower mortality but slowing breath has not been shown to extend life.

verse.reading: Becoming a snake at the root of ஆ, spreading its hood in the field of bliss, folding in at the root of ஊ, running and stretching out the tongue of வ: when the Siddha snake-charmer taught the mantra in which சீ lay, we cut the root of birth in ம and passed beyond maya's bonds.
verse.nuance: The syllables are the cipher: ஆ, ஊ and ம give the pranava's a, u and m, and வ and சீ the letters of சிவ in the five-letter mantra. Tradition takes the snake as the coiled power rising through the syllables. சித்தப்பிடாரனார், the Siddha snake-charmer, is the guru and also Pambatti's own name.

verse.reading: I am not the monkey's young, which holds on by itself; a dog, though I know the custom, what can I do with a mind that keeps on thinking? Drive the evil from me and, like the cat that carries its kitten when they part, you are the one who belongs to my father, Lord of Kailasa.
verse.nuance: The pair of images is the later Vaishnava and Saiva figure for two kinds of grace: the monkey's cub clings to its mother by its own effort, the kitten is carried by the cat. The poet says he is not the clinging cub, so must be carried. மந்திக் குருளை அத்தேன் இல்லை is read as 'I am not that (cub)'; the text is loose, and எந்தைக்கு உரியவன் (the one who belongs to my father) is obscure, perhaps 'you who are mine as a father'.

finding.claim: Expectation and conditioning engage opioid, dopamine and prefrontal systems to produce real changes in pain and symptoms, chiefly in subjective outcomes.

verse.reading: When will the ruinous maya go and cease? When will the scattered mind come straight? When will I stand free of the infatuation that joins the woman with sword-like eyes? Mind, alas! When will all the desire for this hard world be cut at the root? Leaving the planet-like instruments you keep thinking on, look upward; and what it is that joins there, look at the root to see.
verse.nuance: Each எப்போ (when) is addressed to the mind, in the manner of the Pattinathar and Pambatti laments. கருவி (instruments) is the Siddhanta word for the tattvas, and கோளான, planet-like, makes them fates that circle one. The answer given is a direction: மேலே நோக்கி, மூலம் பாரே, look up and look at the root, the mooladhara, which the next work (ch 84) takes up at length.

finding.claim: Maximum human lifespan appears to have plateaued near 115-125 years, and radical life extension in this century is judged implausible.

verse.reading: With the Himalaya's daughter inseparable on one side like an emerald creeper on a coral mountain, with a face like a thousand suns rising from the waves, her young breasts, lotus face, crescent brow, red-lily mouth and lotus hands holding the pot of nectar, and her blue-lily eyes blooming with your splendour, you sat at the Lord's ease in Kazhumalam of the brahmins, which floated above the nagas' land when the upper worlds sank below and stood as the one support of the three worlds in the flood; and when the brahmin child who came with his father, at the toddling age, cried 'Mother' from hunger, she stood before him and gave him the ball of milk kneaded with the food of knowledge; and when the brahmin angrily asked who gave it, the boy pointed with his hand and said he would show him, 'the one with the earring, the one with the bull': there you appeared in grace.
verse.nuance: The second half is the Sambandar legend told in the child's own words, தோடுடைய செவியன் and பீடுடைய பெம்மான் echoing his first Tevaram hymn; ஞான போனகம், the food of knowledge, names the milk as the source of his poetry. The Lord addressed throughout is the one who 'appeared' (வெளிப்பட்டருளினை), so the long praise of Uma leads to his epiphany, not hers.

finding.claim: Meditation programmes produce moderate improvements in anxiety, depression and pain, with low or no evidence of benefit for attention, mood or sleep beyond active controls.

verse.reading: Would anyone trust this birth, my heart, while the hoard lies there and the wife is at the door, having seen, as in a dream, the hiccup, the clenched teeth, the eyes rolled up, the cotton stuffed in, and the bag choke, die and empty itself?
verse.nuance: The first of four venbas (420 to 423) on the same frame: a question to the heart about birth, then கண்டு, having seen, and a death scene. Here the scene is the deathbed itself, each symptom a word, with the cotton (பஞ்சு) stuffed in the nostrils of the corpse.

finding.claim: Nasal breathing entrains oscillations in olfactory and limbic brain areas and improves memory and fear recognition timed to inhalation, an effect absent with mouth breathing.

verse.reading: The letter Sivayam is the letter in which Siva dwells, the true letter to trust as the means; the breath that has gone out through the doorless gate, the five letters Sivaya will call back by that means.
verse.nuance: கபாடமற்ற வாசல் (the gate with no door) is taken as the nostrils or the opening at the crown through which the breath leaves. The claim that the mantra calls the departed breath back is read by tradition as the mantra governing the breath (vaasi) in life, or as restoring life; the verse states it flatly as உபாயம், the means.

finding.claim: Reciting a rosary prayer or a yoga mantra slows breathing to about six a minute and raises baroreflex sensitivity, linking repetitive recitation to the slow-breath physiology.
